facts.statement: Titanoceratops is considered one of the largest known horned dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Titanoceratops was named for its large size, being one of the largest known horned dinosaurs

facts.statement: Titanoceratops had an estimated length of 6.8 meters and a weight of 6.55 tonnes.
facts.quote: With an estimated weight of 6.55 t and length of 6.8 m, Titanoceratops was comparable in size with the largest ceratopsians, Torosaurus and Triceratops

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Titanoceratops was collected in July 1941 from either the upper Fruitland Formation or the lower Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype of Titanoceratops was collected from the upper Fruitland Formation or the lower Kirtland Formation in July 1941

facts.statement: Nicholas R. Longrich classified Titanoceratops within the subgroup Triceratopsini as a close relative of Triceratops based on unique skull features.
facts.quote: Longrich believed that unique features found in the skull reveal it to have been a close relative of Triceratops, classified within the subgroup Triceratopsini.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Titanoceratops is not a distinct genus but rather an unusually large and old specimen of Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: However, other researchers have expressed skepticism, and believe Titanoceratops to simply be an unusually large, old specimen of Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: In 2021, Sebastian Dalman and colleagues classified Titanoceratops as a member of Triceratopsini and a sister taxon to Ojoceratops.
facts.quote: In 2021, Sebastian Dalman and colleagues recovered Titanoceratops as a member of the Triceratopsini, specifically as a sister taxon of Ojoceratops.

facts.statement: In 2020, Denver Fowler and Elizabeth Freedman Fowler suggested that the unique features of Titanoceratops were likely due to advanced age and large size rather than distinct genus status.
facts.quote: In 2020, Denver Fowler and Elizabeth Freedman Fowler critically re-evaluated the evidence that Titanoceratops was a distinct genus. They agreed with Lehman's original assessment, that the features in the specimen that appeared unique were likely due simply to advanced age and unusually large size.

facts.statement: Titanoceratops lived between 74 and 73 million years ago during the late Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Therefore, Titanoceratops dates between 74 and 73 million years ago.

facts.statement: Titanoceratops lived during the Kirtlandian land-vertebrate age, a time characterized by the appearance of Pentaceratops sternbergii.
facts.quote: The age Titanoceratops lived in is called the Kirtlandian land-vertebrate age, and it is characterized by the appearance of Pentaceratops sternbergii.

facts.statement: Titanoceratops was a giant chasmosaurine that lived in what is now New Mexico during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Era un casmosaurino gigantesco que vivió durante el período Cretácico Superior en lo que ahora es Nuevo México

facts.statement: Titanoceratops was formally named by Nicholas R. Longrich in 2011, with the type species Titanoceratops ouranos.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio fue formalmente nombrado por Nicholas R. Longrich en el año 2011 y su especie tipo es Titanoceratops ouranos.

facts.statement: Before its formal description, fossils of Titanoceratops were previously assigned to the genus Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: Con anterioridad, sus fósiles habían sido asignados a Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: Titanoceratops was named for its large size and is considered one of the largest known horned dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Titanoceratops recibió su nombre por su gran tamaño, siendo uno de los dinosaurios con cuernos más grandes conocidos

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2011 by Nicholas R. Longrich based on a specimen previously referred to Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado en 2011 por Nicholas R. Longrich por un espécimen previamente referido a Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: Longrich believed unique skull features indicated Titanoceratops was a close relative of Triceratops, placing it in the Triceratopsini subgroup.
facts.quote: Longrich creía que las características únicas encontradas en el cráneo revelaban que era un pariente cercano de Triceratops, clasificado dentro del subgrupo Triceratopsini.

facts.statement: Some researchers debate the classification, suggesting Titanoceratops is merely an unusually large and old specimen of Pentaceratops rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, otros investigadores han expresado su escepticismo y creen que Titanoceratops es simplemente un espécimen inusualmente grande y viejo de Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: The type species T. ouranos was named in honor of Uranus, Ouranos, the father of the Greek Titans.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue nombrada T. ouranos, en honor a Urano, Ouranos, el padre de los titanes griegos.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen OMNH 10165 is a partial skeleton including mostly complete skulls and jaws, along with much of the rest of the skeleton.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo es OMNH 10165, un esqueleto parcial que incluye un cráneo y mandíbulas en su mayoría completos y gran parte del esqueleto.

facts.statement: The reconstructed skull measures 2.65 meters in length, making it a candidate for the longest skull of any land animal.
facts.quote: El cráneo está incompleto, pero tal como está reconstruido actualmente, mide 2,65 metros de largo, lo que lo convierte en candidato para el cráneo más largo de cualquier animal terrestre.

facts.statement: With an estimated weight of 6.55 tonnes and a length of 6.8 meters, Titanoceratops was comparable in size to the largest ceratopsians, Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: Con un peso estimado de 6,55 toneladas y una longitud de 6,8 metros, Titanoceratops era comparable en tamaño con los ceratopsianos más grandes, Torosaurus y Triceratops

facts.statement: The skull measures 1.2 meters from the snout tip to the squamosal, while the restored frill extends the total length to 2.65 meters.
facts.quote: El cráneo mide 1,2 metros desde la punta del hocico hasta el cuadrado, y el volante restaurado extiende su longitud hasta 2,65 metros

facts.statement: Titanoceratops was as large as later triceratopsines like Triceratops and Torosaurus, with an estimated weight of 6.55 tonnes and a mounted skeleton 6.8 meters long and 2.5 meters high at the rear.
facts.quote: Titanoceratops era tan grande como los triceratopsínidos posteriores Triceratops y Torosaurus , con un peso estimado de 6,55 toneladas y un esqueleto montado que medía 6,8 metros de largo y 2,5 metros de alto en la parte posterior.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul provided a lower size estimate of 6.5 meters in length and 4.5 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: En 2016 , Gregory S. Paul dio una estimación más baja de 6,5 metros y 4,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton includes a partial skull with jaws, synsacral, cervical, dorsal, and sacral vertebrae, caudal vertebrae, ribs, humerus, right radius, femur, tibiae, right fibula, both ilia, both ischia, and ossified tendons.
facts.quote: El esqueleto holotipo de Titanoceratops consta de un cráneo parcial con mandíbulas, vértebras sincervicales, cervicales, dorsales y sacras, vértebras caudales, costillas, húmeros, radio derecho, fémur, tibias, peroné derecho, ambos ilíacos, ambos isquiones y tendones osificados.

facts.statement: The total amount of material assigned to Titanoceratops makes it well-known, comparable to genera such as Triceratops, Vagaceratops, Pentaceratops, Chasmosaurus, Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Anchiceratops.
facts.quote: En total, la cantidad de material asignado a Titanoceratops significa que es bastante conocido, junto con géneros como Triceratops, Vagaceratops, Pentaceratops , Chasmosaurus, Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus y Anchiceratops.

facts.statement: This evidence implies that triceratopsins originally evolved in the south and spread north during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: This implies that the triceratopsins originally evolved in the south, then spread north in the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Titanoceratops is Longrich, 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Longrich, 2011

facts.statement: The species authority for Titanoceratops ouranos is Longrich, 2011.
facts.quote: species_authority: Longrich, 2011

facts.statement: Titanoceratops is classified within the Triceratopsini subgroup.
facts.quote: clasificado dentro del subgrupo Triceratopsini.

facts.statement: The holotype of Titanoceratops was collected in July 1941 from the upper Fruitland Formation or lower Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Titanoceratops fue recolectado de la Formación Fruitland superior o de la Formación Kirtland inferior en julio de 1941

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of most of the fore and hind limbs, some vertebrae, a fairly complete skull with only a small section of the frill, and partial lower jaws.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo consta de la mayor parte de las extremidades anteriores y posteriores, algunas vértebras, un cráneo bastante completo con solo una pequeña sección del volante y mandíbulas inferiores parciales

facts.statement: The genus name Titanoceratops is derived from Greek words meaning "Titan" (a mythical race of giants), "horn", and "face".
facts.quote: El nombre Titanoceratops se deriva del griego Titán, una raza mítica de gigantes, keras, κέρας, que significa "cuerno", y ops, ὤψ, "cara"

facts.statement: The species name T. ouranos refers to Uranus, the father of the race of Titans.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie T. ouranos , se refiere a Urano, el padre de la raza de los titanes

facts.statement: Longrich interpreted that the specimen shared more characteristics with Triceratops and Torosaurus than with Pentaceratops and named a new group, Triceratopsini, to contain them all.
facts.quote: Longrich interpretó que el espécimen compartía más características con Triceratops y Torosaurus que con Pentaceratops y nombró un nuevo grupo, Triceratopsini, para contenerlos a todos

facts.statement: Lehman ignored Longrich's reclassification in his own subsequent publications.
facts.quote: Lehman ignoró la reclasificación de Longrich en sus propias publicaciones posteriores

facts.statement: In a 2020 study, Fowler and Freedman Fowler critically reevaluated the evidence that Titanoceratops was a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Como parte de un estudio de 2020 realizado por Fowler y Freedman Fowler, los autores revaluaron críticamente la evidencia de que Titanoceratops era un género distinto

facts.statement: Fowler and Freedman Fowler agreed with Lehman's original assessment that the specimen's unique characteristics were likely due simply to advanced age and unusually large size.
facts.quote: Estuvieron de acuerdo con la evaluación original de Lehman de que las características del espécimen que parecían únicas probablemente se debieron simplemente a la edad avanzada y al tamaño inusualmente grande

facts.statement: Pending a full reevaluation by other researchers, Fowler and Freedman Fowler opted to consider OMNH 10165 simply as a large Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: En espera de una revaluación completa del espécimen por parte de otros investigadores, Fowler y Freedman Fowler optaron por considerar a OMNH 10165 simplemente como un gran Pentaceratops

facts.statement: Titanoceratops lived between 74 and 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: Titanoceratops data de hace entre 74 y 73 millones de años

facts.statement: The Fruitland Formation is about 100 meters thick and consists of sandstones, shales, and abundant coals deposited in a coastal alluvial plain.
facts.quote: La Formación Fruitland tiene unos 100 metros de espesor y consiste en areniscas, lutitas y abundantes carbones depositados en una llanura aluvial costera

facts.statement: Fossil trees are abundant in the area where the holotype was collected, suggesting a humid and well-wooded environment.
facts.quote: Los árboles fósiles abundan en el área de donde se recolectó el holotipo, lo que sugiere un ambiente húmedo y bien arbolado

facts.statement: A moderately diverse fauna is known from the Kirtland and Fruitland formations.
facts.quote: Se conoce una fauna moderadamente diversa de las formaciones Kirtland y Fruitland

facts.statement: Known dinosaurs from the Fruitland and Kirtland formations include theropods such as Bistahieversor sealeyi, "Saurornitholestes" robustus, Paronychodon lacustris, and an indeterminate ornithomimid.
facts.quote: Entre los dinosaurios conocidos de las formaciones Fruitland y Kirtland se encuentran los terópodos Bistahieversor sealeyi, anteriormente Daspletosaurus sp. y Albertosaurus sp., "Saurornitholestes" robustus, Paronychodon lacustris y un ornitomímido indeterminado

facts.statement: Titanoceratops supports the idea that Late Cretaceous dinosaur faunas were highly endemic.
facts.quote: Titanoceratops apoya la idea de que las faunas de dinosaurios del Cretácico tardío eran altamente endémicas

facts.statement: However, several subsequent studies have cast doubt on the hypothesis that Titanoceratops is a triceratopsinid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, varios estudios posteriores han puesto en duda la hipótesis de que Titanoceratops es un triceratopsínido

facts.statement: The genus Titanoceratops was named by Longrich in 2011.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Titanoceratops (genus), Longrich 2011

facts.statement: The parent group of Titanoceratops is Triceratopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Triceratopsini

facts.statement: Titanoceratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Titanoceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
